anomalies.observed: R4 is a 0 Ω part directly between the signal pins of the two servo headers (Net-(J11-Pin_3) and Net-(J7-Pin_3)). Each signal pin is also driven through a 1 kΩ series resistor from a different bus GPIO group (R15 from the pin 20/22 node, R16 from the pin 19/21 node). In PWM mode this shorts two independent PWM outputs together.
anomalies.expected: Per the spec, R4 is a 1 kΩ series resistor from the PWM2 GPIO net to the channel-2 servo signal pin, and it must not short the two servo signal lines. Serial-mode bridging is supposed to come only from the R13/R14 jumper pair.

evidence.quote: | R3, R4 | 1k each | Series resistors from the PWM1/PWM2 GPIO nets to J3 pin 3 / J8 pin 3 respectively. |

anomalies.impact: The two servo channels are electrically tied together. Two different GPIO PWM outputs fight on one node, so both servos receive the same or corrupted pulse train. The shared node can also overload the GPIO drivers, and PWM mode cannot work as intended.

anomalies.observed: R13 (2.2k) runs from +3V3 to the MAX3485 B line, and R14 (2.2k) runs from the B line to GND. This forms a mid-rail bias divider. Neither resistor reaches a servo signal pin, so the B line has no connection to the servo headers.
anomalies.expected: Per the spec, R13 and R14 are 0 Ω jumpers that bridge the servo signal pins (J3 pin 3 / J8 pin 3) onto the MAX3485 TTL bus in serial mode. They should not be 2.2 kΩ bias resistors tied to the supply rails.

evidence.quote: | R13, R14 | 0 Ω (jumpers) | When shorted, bridge J3-pin3 and J8-pin3 together and onto the MAX3485 TTL bus — schematic note: "Short R13, R14 for Serial Servo". |

anomalies.impact: In serial mode the MAX3485 B terminal is not connected to the servo bus, so the half-duplex serial servo link is broken or biased incorrectly. The resistive divider also draws a standing current from the 3V3 rail.
